(1) As OWNER (owner@sharma.com), left sidebar shows [data-testid=nav-settings]; clicking it navigates to /settings. The page renders [data-testid=settings-money-card] with settings-currency (INR default), settings-threshold (50000 default), settings-signoff-toggle (off), and settings-save button. Screenshot captured. (2) Changed currency INR→USD, threshold 50000→100000, toggled signoff ON, clicked Save → 'Settings saved' success toast appeared. Reloaded /settings — form re-loaded with USD / 100000 / signoff=ON, confirming values persisted via tenant on /auth/me. Then reset to INR/50000/OFF and re-verified persistence — demo state restored so future capture flows use sensible defaults. (3) OWNER-ONLY gate: signed out, signed in as sales@sharma.com (Priya Nair, role=sales) — [data-testid=nav-settings] count=0 in sidebar (correctly hidden by NAV filter `!n.ownerOnly || user?.role==='owner'` in Layout.js:74). Backend is the security boundary as designed.

critical_code_review_comments: App.js line 68 — /settings is wrapped only in <Protected> (auth check), not an owner-only guard. A signed-in non-owner can navigate directly by URL and see the form pre-populated (values leak: tenant currency + threshold + signoff toggle state are visible). This isn't a security bug since the backend PATCH is `require_role('owner')` and returns 403, but it's a mild information disclosure of your workspace's high-value threshold / owner-signoff config to any team member who types /settings. Consider adding an <OwnerOnly> guard component (or extending Protected with an `ownerOnly` prop) that redirects non-owners to `/` or shows the 403 page you already use. Same treatment as `ownerOnly:true` in NAV.

Settings.js line 12-15 — initial state is derived from `tenant` synchronously in useState. If a user navigates to /settings BEFORE AuthContext finishes hydrating tenant (edge case: hard refresh with slow /auth/me), the form initializes with fallback defaults (50000/false/INR) and never updates when tenant loads later — the form would show stale defaults. Fix: use a useEffect that resyncs state when `tenant?.high_value_threshold` / `tenant?.currency` / `tenant?.require_owner_signoff` change, OR guard the render with `if (!tenant) return <Loading/>`. In practice AuthContext blocks the entire router with a loading state so this may not repro, but the pattern is fragile.

Settings.js line 20 — threshold validation only catches NaN and negative. Missing: (a) upper bound sanity check (a fat-finger '100000000' silently persists and effectively disables the high-value flag), (b) integer coercion — `parseFloat` allows 50000.5 which is a currency ambiguity for INR. Suggest `parseInt` + max like 1e9, and show inline validation error rather than only toast.

Settings.js line 57-60 — the help paragraph mixes an inline <span> ('verify before approving') between plain text spans, and the flex layout with `items-start` + `gap-1.5` produces two visible whitespace gaps in the rendered sentence (see design_issues). Cleanest fix: put the whole sentence in one text block with `<span className='font-semibold'>` inline, no flex wrapper — just position the Info icon absolutely or with a leading inline-block.

Settings.js — no explicit loading state for the FIRST render before tenant is hydrated. If refreshTenant() has a network hiccup after Save, the toast still shows 'Settings saved' but local state is what user typed; a subsequent reload will authoritatively reflect server truth. Consider awaiting refreshTenant BEFORE showing the success toast so the visible state is provably synced.

Settings.js line 23 — the PATCH payload uses camelCase-mixed field names `high_value_threshold` / `require_owner_signoff` / `currency`. Confirmed matching the backend. Just noting for future consistency: rest of the codebase uses snake_case for API fields — this file follows convention correctly. No action.

Settings.js line 63-72 — the sign-off toggle is a <button> with a checkbox-lookalike inside. Missing `role='switch'` + `aria-checked` for accessibility. Screen readers announce it as a plain button. Add `aria-pressed={signoff}` or restructure as a real checkbox for a11y.

Layout.js line 49 — the ownerOnly flag on NAV works, but bottom mobile nav (BOTTOM_NAV, line 53-59) does not include Settings at all, meaning mobile owners have to open the drawer to reach Settings. Fine for phase-1 but worth noting for mobile-heavy owners.

Settings.js — no dirty-state tracking. If a user edits values then navigates away without saving, changes are silently lost. Consider `useBeforeUnload` or a route-block prompt when form is dirty. Low priority for phase-1.
action_items: OPTIONAL/NICE-TO-HAVE: Add a client-side owner-only guard on the /settings route (App.js:68) — either an <OwnerOnly> wrapper or extend <Protected role='owner'>. Currently non-owners can view the form (populated with tenant values) but cannot save (backend 403). Not a security bug, but avoids information leakage of the owner's threshold/signoff config.
OPTIONAL/POLISH: Fix the help-text layout under threshold input (Settings.js line 57-60) — the inline flex around the sentence introduces visible whitespace gaps. Simplify to a single text block.
OPTIONAL/A11Y: Add `role='switch'` + `aria-checked={signoff}` to the signoff toggle button in Settings.js (line 63).
